transcript.text: Alright everyone, we've got a stability sprint coming up — ten business days, capacity for one primary technical-debt focus. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our normal round-robin check-in. We've got three candidates in the backlog: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Let's hear from backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support on which of these they think should be the priority and why. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet, but this is highly relevant to the decision — legacy_csv_exporter is much closer to completion than the board likely reflects.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we decide. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was verifying scanner results and haven't filed the security finding yet, but this is an active vulnerability in a component we're considering for the sprint focus. Combined with what Devon just shared — that only two endpoint migrations remain and they're completable this sprint — I'd strongly recommend legacy_csv_exporter as the sprint focus. We'd be closing a security vulnerability and finishing a near-complete migration in the same ten-day window.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something important to add from the customer support side. During a customer call this morning, I confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior. Those accounts will need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. I recorded the call in a support note that hasn't synced to the sprint-planning system yet, so this wouldn't be visible to anyone looking at the board. This is directly relevant: if we choose legacy_csv_exporter as the sprint focus, we need to account for producing that migration guide as part of the work, or we risk breaking audit workflows for those 42 enterprise customers.
transcript.speaker: A4

Upgrade the legacy_csv_exporter dependency from libxml 3.9.4 to the approved remediation target libxml 4.1.0, resolving the known exploitable parsing vulnerability.
Produce and distribute a migration guide covering the old audit-column behavior changes for the 42 enterprise accounts that depend on the legacy behavior, before enabling the new behavior.
Update the planning board to reflect the current migration status, the security finding, and the customer support note so the sprint plan is fully documented.
